scope: The actual finite-dimensional epsilon LayerNorm uses the arithmetic mean and population variance (division by d), preserves input-dependent statistics, and permits arbitrary signed learned gamma and beta. For epsilon>0, layerNormPair_exact proves recovery for every real input-stream pair; value_variancePair and layerVariance_nonnegative derive the inverse-square-root precondition. The companion layerNormPair_regular proves convexity, coordinatewise monotonicity, and nonnegative values on any convex domain where the incoming pairs have those properties. The source assumes d>=1; the formal d=0 coordinate conclusions are vacuous. This link covers the complete LayerNorm recipe and ordinary displayed formula, not the full Transformer theorem.
secondary_findings: No substantive mismatch; exact signed gain/bias and population variance; regularity correctly conditional on incoming Regular pairs.
